Seven classrooms, a DAF truck and a Toyota Camry have been destroyed by fire following an outbreak at an NNPC filling station along Command-Ekoro Road, Alimosho, Lagos State. The fire also destroyed three fuel dispensing pumps and electrical appliances in the affected classrooms. The Toyota Camry had registration number EKY 430 JS. PUNCH Metro learnt that the inferno reportedly started while a tanker was discharging diesel at the filling station before spreading to the adjoining St. Lawrence Greater Height School. The Lagos State Emergency Management Agency disclosed this in a statement signed by its Permanent Secretary, Dr Olufemi Oke-Osanyintolu, on Monday. According to Oke-Osanyintolu, LASEMA’s Igando-based Beta Team was deployed to the scene after receiving a distress call. He said preliminary investigations indicated that the fire started from a tanker while discharging diesel before spreading to the filling station’s dispensing pumps and the adjoining school building. The Government, however, acknowledges with deep sympathy the material losses recorded,” he stated. Oke-Osanyintolu said the combined efforts of LASEMA, the Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service, the National Emergency Management Agency, the Lagos State Ambulance Service, the Lagos State Traffic Management Authority, the Lagos Neighbourhood Safety Corps and police officers from the Ile-Iwe Division led to the successful extinguishing of the fire. Meanwhile, he disclosed that the agency also responded to two other emergencies in different parts of the state on the same day. Plateau newlyweds die in fire, probe begins Dangote, Sinotruk unveil electric truck Polaris Bank deepens commitment to girl-child education In another incident at Alaro City, along the Epe Expressway, a tanker conveying 45,000 litres of Premium Motor Spirit overturned after its driver reportedly lost control while attempting to avoid a Dangote truck overtaking it at close range. The tanker had registration number AKD-387YK. According to Oke-Osanyintolu, no casualty was recorded, while firefighters applied foam to the tanker to prevent a possible fire outbreak. He added that the petroleum product was subsequently transferred to another tanker before the overturned vehicle was recovered. In a separate incident, a Mack tipper broke down at Ladipo Bus Stop, inward Ikeja, following a mechanical fault involving its shaft, obstructing vehicular movement. Oke-Osanyintolu said the response team worked with LASTMA to divert traffic and deployed heavy-duty equipment to remove the vehicle from the road. “The Response Team, alongside the Lagos State Traffic Management Authority, diverted oncoming vehicles to prevent secondary accidents, while the Agency’s heavy-duty equipment, Super Metro, was deployed for recovery. The broken-down tipper was successfully recovered off the road and parked at a layby, thereby ensuring free vehicular movement, and the operation was concluded with the Response Team and equipment returning to base in good condition,” he stated. He added that the Lagos State Government urged filling station operators, tanker drivers and motorists to observe safety regulations, ensure regular vehicle maintenance and avoid speeding and dangerous overtaking. The government also appealed to school owners and managers to maintain clear emergency access routes and cooperate with emergency responders. “The Lagos State Government uses this moment to appeal passionately to filling station operators, tanker drivers and motorists to adhere strictly to safety protocols, particularly during the discharge of petroleum products, ensure regular maintenance of vehicles, avoid speeding and dangerous overtaking, and remain vigilant at all times,” he added.
